subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should Telegram outbound local media roots be exposed through a narrow channel/media config key, through the broader `tools.fs.roots` policy, or not exposed beyond managed staging roots?
rationale: The schema/runtime gap is source-provable, but any fix expands which host-local paths can be read and uploaded through a channel, so automation should not choose the permanent security boundary.

options.title: Unify Under A Root Policy
options.body: Use the broader filesystem/media-root policy, or a narrowed successor, as the single operator-controlled contract across Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

options.title: Add A Telegram/Media Key
options.body: Expose a narrow allowlist such as `channels.telegram.mediaLocalRoots` with strict validation, docs, and channel-specific tests if maintainers want a smaller escape hatch.

options.title: Keep Staging Only
options.body: Decline new configurable roots and document managed media/workspace staging as the supported safety boundary.

recommendation.title: Unify Under A Root Policy
recommendation.body: Use the broader filesystem/media-root policy, or a narrowed successor, as the single operator-controlled contract across Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits across media-root policy, Telegram send behavior, and gateway send paths where history shows substantial adjacent ownership.
